fields.disappearance: 1890, in Vṛndāvana, four or five days after seeing off Rādhikānātha Gosvāmī at Mathurā (the record's text)
fields.place: Born at Guḍapāḍā (Citāhāṭī), Kutugrāma, near Katwa; Katwa (Gaurāṅga's temple); Vṛndāvana (Madana-mohana Ṭhaurā), with his samādhi
fields.guru: Vinodīlāla Ṭhākura of Faridpur, Nadia (Kṛṣṇa-dīkṣā); Siddha Caitanya dāsa Bābājī (dīkṣā, by the Sadguru-saṅga); Siddha Nityānanda dāsa Bābājī of Madana-mohana Ṭhaurā (veśa)
fields.disciples: Advaita dāsa (Annadāprasāda Rāya, later Giridhārī dāsa Bābājī); Haricaraṇa dāsa (Mahendranātha Bhaṭṭācārya)
fields.notes: A great paṇḍita of a Śākta brāhmaṇa family near Katwa, grandson of Guruprasāda Mukhopādhyāya Vidyānidhi; wife Rāmadāsī; sons Rasavallabha Bhaktibhūṣaṇa and Vaiṣṇavacaraṇa Bhāgavatabhūṣaṇa. Turned to the Gauḍīya books in the company of the Vaiṣṇavas of Katwa; went to Vṛndāvana, took veśa from Siddha Nityānanda dāsa Bābājī; famous for his humility (bowing to everyone, even animals). Saved Annadāprasāda Rāya from turning Christian and initiated him as Advaita dāsa. Died in Vṛndāvana in 1890.

fields.name: Vaṁśī dāsa Bābājī
fields.aka: Vaṁśī Dāsa Bābājī, Vamsidasa Bābājī, Bhairavacandra (birth name)
fields.place: Born at Majitpura (Kiśoraganj, Mymensingh); Navadvīpa (Caumuhanī, Jhāutalā, north of Bāḍāla ghāṭ); Vṛndāvana; back to Mymensingh at the end
fields.guru: Of the family line of Narottama Ṭhākura (his guru's name is not given)
fields.disciples: Dāmodara and Bihārī (followers from Mymensingh); Manohara dāsa, Govinda dāsa, Jagadbandhu dāsa
fields.notes: Born Bhairavacandra, son of Sanātana Malobrahma of Majitpura (Mymensingh). The great avadhūta of Navadvīpa, living with his Deities Gaura-Nitāi, Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa and Lāḍḍu-Gopāla in vātsalya; honoured by Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī, whom he called «Jagannāthera Bimalā». Over ninety in the early 1940s; went back to Mymensingh and left this world there.

fields.place: Born at Gaṅgānandapur near Jhikargāchā (Jessore), close to Śrīpāṭa Bodhkhānā; Calcutta (Bāgbāzār, Kālīghāṭ); Kāśī (Gaṇeśa-mahallā by Brahma-kuṇḍa)
fields.guru: None is given: the order to chant «Haribol» came to him from the goddess at Kālīghāṭ
fields.notes: Born Navīncandra Bhaṭṭācārya; a village schoolteacher till forty. Fell at the feet of everyone in Calcutta until they said «Haribol»; led the street saṅkīrtana during the plague with Kṣetranātha Mallik; most of his disciples were poor and low-caste, named after Mahāprabhu's associates. His disciple Vipina Bihārī Caṭṭopādhyāya (#1695) held him to be Advaita Ācārya. Died on Varāha-dvādaśī.
